stories.name: Marcus (composite)
stories.label: Composite story built from 3 sourced recruiting paths
basis: An undersized high school lineman with no D1 offers chose a D3 school after it pitched its academic path (Ali Marpet, Hobart) (https://www.buccaneers.com/news/reflecting-on-ali-marpet-s-college-career-16779250)

A family weighed a guaranteed option against a long shot at a bigger program (Hunter Renfrow, Clemson) (https://www.ncaa.com/news/football/article/2017-01-10/college-football-hunter-renfrows-leap-faith-carried-him-clemson)

A D3 recruit picked his school after a campus tour and being recruited by the head coach (Elias Espinosa, Conn College) (https://nescac.com/news/2024/12/20/nescac-news-nescac-friday-feature-elias-espinosa-conn-college-mens-basketball.aspx)

rule.text: Division III: paid official visits open January 1 of junior year. D3 offers no athletic scholarships; aid there is academic and need-based.

beats: Composite story, built from three sourced recruiting paths. Marcus is not a real person; every image of him is an illustration. He is a two-way lineman at a mid-size public school, a little light for his position, with good grades and no Division I offers.
His family asks what many football families ask: is there a real college roster for a player who is not the size the big programs list, and what does it cost if there is no athletic money?

In this composite, Marcus stops waiting on Division I and asks Division III coaches about both football and his intended major. He tours campuses and goes with the coach who recruits him directly, a pattern drawn from the sources below.

The rule that mattered. Division III: paid official visits open January 1 of junior year. D3 offers no athletic scholarships; aid there is academic and need-based. (D3 Bylaw 13.6.1.1.1). The rule did not cause this outcome and guarantees nothing. Check it yourself at the source.

He picks a Division III school where he can play and study what he came for. Aid is academic and need-based, not athletic. He plays four seasons, mostly as a starter in his last two, and graduates. No draft, no headline. That is the destination, not a consolation.

One path, made of several real ones, not a formula. This person does not exist, and the ending is ordinary on purpose: most college athletes play, study and graduate. Nothing here proves a playbook, camp or service causes a result. We do not contact coaches, and we never contact your kid.

stories.name: Jasmine (composite)

basis: A family sent a highlight video to about 25 junior-college and D2 schools when no D1 offers came (Derrick White) (https://www.nba.com/spurs/derrick-white-dare-be-great)

NAIA recruiting has few restrictions on contact between athletes and coaches (NAIA guide for college-bound students) (https://www.naia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/naia_guide_college_bound_student-1.pdf)

rule.text: NAIA: register with the NAIA Eligibility Center (PlayNAIA.org). A 2.3 high school GPA makes a freshman eligible, or two of three: ACT 18/SAT 970, 2.0 GPA, top half of class. NAIA publishes no contact-date calendar.
rule.bylaw: NAIA Bylaws Art. V Sec. C, 2026-27 NAIA Handbook p.70
